d54c042592da6247: SEREMBAN: Bukit Aman today completed recording statements from 10 former Negri Sembilan exco members and several others over the state's constitutional crisis.

The former exco members were seen leaving the Negri Sembilan Islamic Religious Council (MAINS) Tower here around 2pm after spending nearly three hours having their statements recorded by Bukit Aman's Classified Criminal Investigation Unit.
The police team left the building around 2.15pm after the statement-recording session, which began at about 11am.
However, the session did not involve Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim.
Former state Industry, Technology, Innovation and Digital exco Datuk Mohd Asna Amin said the statements were recorded separately, with each session taking about 30 to 35 minutes.
"Many Bukit Aman officers came, but none of them were intimidating, and we fully cooperated. For now, they are only recording our statements.
"More than 60 questions were asked and answered, all relating mainly to the crisis that is unfolding. Negri Sembilan is unique because its state constitution is different from those of other states.
"The Negri Sembilan State Constitution 1959 (UUTKNS) serves as the guide. We answered based on what we know," he told reporters at the tower's lobby here today.
Asna, who is also Lenggeng assemblyman, said they were informed that the statement-recording exercise could also involve other officials who may be called in.
He said Bukit Aman would inform them if further statements were required.

"We were informed that follow-up statements would be recorded if necessary," he said, adding that the authorities had not specified any particular provisions under which the statements were being recorded.

The statements are believed to be linked to the state's political crisis following the revocation of the 10 exco members' appointments by Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
The revocation came a week after the exco members issued a joint statement allegedly confirming Tuanku Muhriz's removal as state ruler.
The Negri Sembilan palace previously said the exco members had breached their oath of office and allegiance to the ruler, which they swore on Aug 7.
On Thursday, Ismail said the 10 former exco members, whom he maintained still legally held office, had been barred from entering their respective offices.
Attorney-General Tan Sri Dusuki Mokhtar had earlier affirmed that the revocation of the exco appointments, seven of whom are from Umno, was valid.
Yesterday, it was reported that the exco members would have their statements recorded.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail had previously said Bukit Aman officers would travel to Negri Sembilan to record their statements.

The 10 former exco members comprise Umno representatives Datuk Mustapha Nagoor (Palong), Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli (Linggi), Datuk Zaiful Bahri Idris (Chembong), Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali (Sungai Lui), Datuk Asna Mohd Amin (Lenggeng), Siti Nur Umaira Hasim (Labu) and Suhaimizan Bizar (Gemencheh).
The other three are MCA representative Siow Kong Choon (Chennah), Pas representative Fairuz Isa (Serting) and Wawasan representative Datuk Razali Abu Samah (Sikamat).

0a09b094e4cbd62b: PUTRAJAYA: Perkongsian perniagaan yang retak membabitkan dana lebih RM2.4 juta berakhir dengan keputusan Mahkamah Persekutuan bahawa rakan usaha sama (JV) boleh menyaman bekas rakan kongsi perniagaannya secara langsung bagi menuntut semula wang yang didakwa telah disalah guna atau dialihkan.
Mahkamah tertinggi membenarkan rayuan Pelorus Holding Sdn Bhd terhadap Jaffa Roger Dawkins, Rabiatul Adawiyyah Mohamad dan Harris Luqman Group Sdn Bhd.

Hakim Mahkamah Persekutuan Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh, yang bersidang bersama-sama Hakim Collin Lawrence Sequerah dan Azimah Omar berkata, Pelorus menguatkuasakan kewajipan kontrak yang terhutang kepadanya di bawah perjanjian usaha sama (JVA).
Syarikat usaha sama itu, Pelorus HLG Sdn Bhd, katanya, sengaja tidak dijadikan pihak dalam JVA itu, walaupun ia telah diperbadankan semasa perjanjian tersebut ditandatangani.
“Ini bukan suatu kecuaian penggubalan ,” kata Wan Ahmad Farid sambil menambah, pihak-pihak terbabit secara sedar memilih mengikat diri mereka secara peribadi di bawah perjanjian itu.
Pelorus sebelum ini menyediakan dana bagi JV membabitkan bekalan ternakan, pertanian bersepadu, pembiakan, operasi rumah sembelih serta produk daging.
Hubungan itu kemudiannya retak dan Pelorus memfailkan saman untuk mendapatkan semula wang yang didakwa haknya.

Antara tuntutannya termasuk RM1.19 juta yang didakwa telah dialihkan untuk manfaat Harris Luqman Group, serta RM1.21 juta lagi yang didahulukan bagi melunaskan pinjaman Agrobank milik syarikat JV itu.

Mahkamah Rayuan sebelum ini memutuskan, wang itu kepunyaan syarikat JV terbabit dan sebarang tuntutan sewajarnya difailkan oleh syarikat itu sendiri atau melalui tindakan derivatif, namun Mahkamah Persekutuan tidak bersetuju dengan pandangan tersebut.
Wan Ahmad Farid berkata, Pelorus bukan sekadar pemegang saham yang mengadu bahawa syarikat JV itu mengalami kerugian.
“Plaintif bukanlah pemegang saham terkilan yang merungut mengenai salah laku terhadap syarikatnya, sebaliknya merupakan pihak berkontrak yang menuntut haknya di bawah JVA yang mengikat,” katanya.
Beliau berkata, Pelorus menuntut pemulangan wangnya sendiri dan menguatkuasakan kewajipan yang telah diikrarkan oleh para defendan secara langsung kepadanya di bawah perjanjian itu.

Mahkamah turut menolak hujah bahawa aturan pembiayaan Pelorus menjurus kepada aktiviti pinjaman wang tanpa lesen, setelah mendapati bahawa wang pendahuluan tersebut disalurkan sebagai sebahagian obligasi kontrak JV itu.
Bagaimanapun, Mahkamah Persekutuan menolak tuntutan berasingan Pelorus berjumlah RM516,972 atas persetujuan bahawa jumlah itu gagal dibuktikan secara wajar.
Tuntutannya sebanyak RM1 juta berdasarkan jaminan peribadi yang diberikan oleh Dawkins dan Rabiatul pula dibenarkan.
Defendan turut diperintahkan membayar kos sebanyak RM100,000.

Peguam David Mathews, S Shaarvin Raaj, K Ravvenneah dan Reuben Choong mewakili Pelorus, manakala Hasshahari Johari Mawi, Rosly Khady Ayub Khan, Shah Nurul Afzan Abdullah serta Nur Amni Irdina Mat Ayob bertindak bagi pihak responden.
a12c7fe2b8fb8e8c: KUALA LUMPUR: Net profit of IOI Properties Group Bhd, Genting Bhd and YTL Corp Bhd is expected to be affected by rising Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yields, with the impact estimated up to two per cent, said BIMB Research.

IOI Properties is expected to be the most sensitive to rising MGS yield, with a 10-basis-point increase in borrowing costs estimated to reduce its 2026 net profit by 1.96 per cent, followed by Genting at 0.93 per cent and YTL Corp at 0.73 per cent.

In a report on Monday, BIMB Research said the shift towards a higher-for-longer interest rate environment could tighten credit conditions for companies with unhedged floating-rate debt, high refinancing requirements and sizeable maturities.
It said 10-year MGS yields had recently climbed as high as 4.18 per cent, compared with the 3.58 per cent average since Jan 2025 and off the low of 3.36 per cent.
"Our house view is for 10-year MGS to hold around 3.90 per cent till end of the year but shift towards 4.00 per cent by end-2027.
"In comparison, we are looking at five per cent 10-year US Treasury by end-2026 and 4.6 per cent by end-2027," it said.
The higher-yield environment follows a surge in corporate borrowing, with non-financial corporate bond and sukuk issuances reaching a record RM216 billion over the 12 months to July.
IOI PROPERTIES MOST EXPOSED
BIMB Research flagged IOI Properties for its high floating-rate exposure, with about 87 per cent of its total debt tied to floating rates based on its latest annual report.
The firm estimated the exposure had risen to more than 90 per cent after gross debt increased 29 per cent to RM25.4 billion as at end-June, pushing net gearing to 0.85 times.
The increase was driven by the South Beach acquisition and is expected to rise further following the RM8 billion acquisition of Asia Square Tower 2 in Singapore in September.

"Most of the debt is tied to three Singapore assets — Central Boulevard (RM8.4 billion) and South Beach (RM6 billion) generate rental income, while Marina View (RM6.6 billion) still requires development funding.
"Together, they represent about 83 per cent of gross borrowings. Management has confirmed that Singapore borrowings carry floating rates based on Singapore Overnight Rate Average," it said in a note.

Based on estimated June 2026 floating-rate borrowings of RM22.98 billion, BIMB Research estimated that a 10-basis-point increase would raise annual cash interest costs by about RM23 million for IOI Properties.

After accounting for capitalised interest at Marina View and a 24 per cent tax shield, BIMB Research estimated a RM13.2 million impact on IOI Properties' net profit, equivalent to 1.34 per cent of its financial year 2027 (FY27) forecast core net profit of RM988 million.
The firm said slower Marina View sales, weaker rental receipts or further investment spending could keep gearing elevated despite earnings growth.
REFINANCING RISKS
For Genting, BIMB Research grouped Genting Bhd and its 74 per cent-owned Genting Malaysia Bhd, noting that both would need to refinance substantial debt over the next 12 months.
Genting's estimated debt that will mature within the next 12 months stood at RM9.1 billion while Genting Malaysia has about RM7.8 billion.
Their net gearing stood at 61.5 per cent and 137 per cent respectively, while net debt-to-EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation) ratios were 4.1 times and 5.2 times.
"It is worth flagging that the finance cost to net profit ratios are also inflated by both stocks' volatile earnings, which have been underperforming and dipping into losses," it said.
For YTL Corp and its 53 per cent-owned YTL Power International Bhd, the firm highlighted high debt, elevated gearing and sizeable maturities, although both have relatively low floating-rate exposure.

YTL Corp and YTL Power had net gearing of 130 per cent and 138 per cent respectively, with gross debt of RM56 billion and RM40 billion. Their net debt-to-EBITDA ratios stood at 4.8 times and 5.7 times.
BIMB Research estimated RM5.4 billion of YTL Corp's debt and RM2.9 billion of YTL Power's debt would mature over the next 12 months.
It also noted that YTL Power's capital expenditure had accelerated to an average of RM1.6 billion per quarter from about RM550 million previously, mainly due to data centre investments in Johor.

"Additionally, with YTL Power in contention for the planting up of new gas-fired power plants (should kick in around 2028), there will be even more demand to be placed on the already levered balance sheet," it added.

The firm said capital-intensive and highly leveraged companies faced greater earnings risks from higher rates, while technology companies were relatively less exposed, with most stocks in its screen in a net cash position.

edf03658db7819f5: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian passport is now ranked second globally in The Passport Index Global Ranking 2026, rising from third last year.
The Immigration Department said that this achievement reflects the strength and international acceptance of the Malaysian passport.

"Based on the ranking, Malaysian passport holders have access to 175 destinations, comprising 129 visa-free destinations and 46 destinations with visa-on-arrival, while 23 destinations require a visa," it said in a social media post.
Based on data from www.passportindex.org, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) passport holds the top spot in the Passport Power Rank, followed by Singapore and Malaysia in second place.
Meanwhile, Spain's passport ranks third, while 16 other countries, including Belgium, Denmark, Germany, Sweden, Italy, Switzerland, Austria, and Norway, share fourth place.
8be48c049a65d596: TEHRAN: State media in Iran on Monday reported that Iran's delegation to the UN General Assembly had no talks planned with the US, after US president Donald Trump said he expected more negotiations.
"Iran's delegation in New York has no plans for negotiations with the US," said the official IRNA news agency, citing an unnamed source close to the group.
Trump told media outlet Axios on Sunday that he expected talks to resume soon, a day after he rejected a proposal by Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days.
"Iran's views and positions were conveyed clearly and explicitly to the US side... via a Qatari mediator," IRNA said, adding that the Iranian delegation would return to Tehran on Tuesday.
Iran says it presented seven conditions for ending the war and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic waterway through which roughly 20% of the world's oil and gas flowed before the war.
The strait lies at the heart of the conflict that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February.
Following that attack, Tehran placed a chokehold on the waterway, and Washington responded with a blockade of Iranian ports.

Axios said indirect talks mediated by Qatar could take place as early as Monday, less than a week after similar discussions between US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi.
Iran demands a seven-day ceasefire across the Middle East, including in Lebanon, where its ally Hezbollah is regularly bombarded by Israel.
It also demands the unfreezing of its foreign assets, lifting sanctions on its oil sector, and an end to the US naval blockade.
Trump rejected their demands on Saturday.
However, fighting has once again slowed as the US has not struck Iran since Sept 1, although vessels have regularly been struck in the Strait of Hormuz.
55f0bd7df8e8c559: KUALA LUMPUR: The right to information as a core component of freedom of speech and expression will be addressed in the Freedom of Information Bill 2026.

Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said Parliamentary Special Select Committee (PSSC) members took note of views that this core principle must be clearly reflected in the bill.
She said the matter will be further examined alongside the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC), particularly from constitutional and legal perspectives.
"Therefore, appropriate space must be given for this matter to be thoroughly studied before any conclusion is drawn regarding the need for constitutional amendments.

"The PSSC also takes note of the need to ensure the public enjoys broad and meaningful access to information held by public authorities, in line with the principles of transparency and accountability.

"In ensuring that access can be effectively implemented while safeguarding interests such as national security and public order, any refusal to disclose information must be based on clear and justifiable grounds," she said at the National Town Hall Session on the Freedom of Information Bill 2026 in Parliament today.

Azalina added that the PSSC will also study an appropriate review mechanism when an application for information is rejected, including whether the function should be carried out through an internal appeal process or placed under the proposed Ombudsman Malaysia.
She stressed that this is crucial to ensure that access to information provided under the law is supported by effective review mechanisms and remedies.
"All technical, structural, and drafting matters raised today will also be examined and refined by the PSSC before any final stance is taken.

"The government remains committed to ensuring that this reform is developed through an inclusive, thorough, and responsible process to produce a strong, balanced, and effective freedom of information framework, thereby strengthening openness, transparency, and accountability in national administration," she said.
Meanwhile, Azalina said today's public hearing session is not the final step, but part of the parliamentary review process.
She said the government does not want to enact legislation merely to state that Malaysia has a freedom of information law.

Instead, she said, the government aims to ensure that the law created is clear regarding rights, exemptions, public authority responsibilities, as well as review and remedy mechanisms available to the public.
abb08730667b5fc5: AICHI: Malaysia's Honor of Kings team are struggling to come to terms with their defeat by China in the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games final, despite acknowledging their opponents as one of the powerhouses of the game.
Team captain Lee Han Siang believes Malaysia had a genuine chance of pulling off an upset, with only fine margins separating the two sides in China's 4-0 victory at Aichi Sky Expo today.
Han Siang said shortcomings in technical execution and strategy made the difference between Malaysia and the gold medal, leaving the team disappointed despite securing silver.
"We are not happy with this result. We felt we could have won because in all four games, we only needed a little bit more to do it. So, we are very disappointed with the result.
"I think we need more training to find the answers and improve our weaknesses," said Han Siang after the match.

Malaysia fielded Chen Tat Yann, Lim Chee Hong, Chong Han Hui, Ryan Na Jie Rong and Han Siang but were unable to contain a well-organised China line-up comprising Huang Yaoqin, Wang Ke, Xu Bicheng, Meng Jiajun and He Weijia.
China, regarded as one of the leading forces in Honor of Kings, produced a consistent performance from the start before sealing the gold medal with a comprehensive victory.
Han Siang, however, said facing China in the final provided Malaysia with valuable lessons as they look to continue developing.
"We learnt a lot from these four games and we will improve ourselves for the next tournament.
"China are still a strong team in Honor of Kings, but Malaysia can improve our game to compete with and challenge them in the future," he said.
The silver medal, nonetheless, Malaysia's target and was the country's third esports medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.
Earlier, e-racing athlete Taj Izrin Aiman Taj Madira won gold in Gran Turismo 7, while Malaysia also secured silver in eFootball.
769ac337b2c8a41b: SINGAPORE, Sept 28 — The late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah was a warm and gracious person, full of life, and had a wonderful sense of humour, said Singapore Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong.
Dr Siti Hasmah, wife of former Prime Minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, passed away at the National Heart Institute (IJN), Kuala Lumpur on Monday morning at the age of 100.

Lee, in expressing his condolences to Dr Mahathir and family, said Dr Siti Hasmah as a doctor had devoted much of her life to improving the health and well-being of Malaysians, particularly women, children, and families.
“Ho Ching and I will remember Tun Siti Hasmah fondly,” he said in his Facebook post on Monday.
Lee also fondly recalled his interaction with Dr Siti Hasmah about her love for music and the violin.
“I remember speaking to Tun Dr Siti Hasmah about her violin performance at the Istana Budaya, when she had played for a good cause.
“She continued performing well into her 90s, including to raise funds for charity. Her zest for life was remarkable,” he said. — Bernama
63ea15cdfa34848b: TAIPEI: When you're rushing to do some last-minute shopping before a flight, checking every single item in your bag isn't always a priority.
​Taiwanese star Jelly Yang recently shared a cautionary tale on Instagram after dropping by an Adidas store in South Korea to grab a pair of trainers right before heading to the airport.
​"The staff opened the box for me to check. I made sure the sizes were correct, and they wrapped everything back up. I was practically on my way to the airport," the 42-year-old wrote.
​However, wanting to save space in her luggage, Yang decided to discard the shoebox.
​"I took the trainers out and, I don't know why, but I suddenly felt the urge to unwrap them properly," she said.
​It turned out to be a stroke of luck.
​Upon taking a closer look, Yang was stunned to discover that the staff had given her two shoes for the exact same foot.
​"I asked the staff to come and take a look, and he was completely shocked as well," she recalled.
​"Thank goodness I decided to open them. Otherwise, how on earth was I supposed to wear them back in Taiwan? I wouldn't have been able to file a complaint either. Absolutely ridiculous!"
e6ccc3d2352e60c6: It's hard to make big sheds symbols of oppression, but the datacenter industry's having a jolly good crack at it. Its big boxes of semi-sentient sand are increasingly seen as satanic sandcastles, environmental disasters that inflict drought while boiling oceans. Their role as dark cathedrals of the equally demonic AIs has done nothing to soften attitudes. A new contract of candour is needed between those who build datacenters and those who despise them. Shrugging off concerns, or offering shiny misdirections with no intent of following through, no longer works. Take energy. Without numbers that can be trusted, it's impossible to judge the environmental effect of using datacenters. How much energy does it take to ask Claude to write a limerick or a database? Who knows. TThere are wildly differing estimates, but nothing reliable enough to inform personal choices or public policy on ethical use. We need to know this not just in broad terms, but with enough accuracy and currency to differentiate between models and hardware generations. The only source of data good enough for this purpose is the datacenter operator. Without that cooperation, nobody's going to believe that anything other than a mad dash for gigawatts at any cost is powering build-out decisions. Given projects such as Musk's xAI Colossus clusters in the Deep South, energized by methane-burning turbines installed with scant regard for regulatory permission, the industry can hardly expect the benefit of the doubt. Lots of lawsuits, though. Then there's the tendency to wave at future nuclear power – and even fusion – as though it excuses burning hydrocarbons today. Nuclear power may eventually shoulder some of the load, but many of the projects now being promoted will not deliver electricity for years. Fusion will be outperformed by slide rules for longer still. This is not an answer to the immediate consequences of the build-out. Meanwhile, we've had pious platitudes that AI is going to get so good it will design itself out of environmental damage. Seen much sign of that lately? Then there's the sector's on-off involvement with genuine innovation. Take the possibilities of marine datacenters powered by tidal and wave generators. The oceans offer abundant cooling and energy, with the tides driven by the gravitational interaction of the Earth, Moon, and Sun. Tidal power in particular is cosmically reliable; we know what the tides will be doing hundreds of years in advance. Seawater is not an ideal coolant, being corrosive and jellyfish-infested, but marine engineers have spent more than a century learning how to work around such problems. As for wave power, there's a lot going on below the radar, although don't wait to hear about it from the big guys. Panthalassa is building wave generators that look disturbingly and fittingly like the spaceship Discovery One from 2001: A Space Odyssey. You know, the home of the most famously insane AI in fiction. The 85-metre structure floats vertically, with a spherical section bobbing at the surface and a long tubular tail extending down through the water column. Wave motion forces internally recirculated water through a turbine, generating electricity for AI hardware inside a sealed, seawater-cooled container. It is designed to operate without anchors, subsea cables or a physical connection to land, avoiding some of the complexity of conventional offshore energy projects. As part of a floating datacenter, it's envisioned that connectivity would be via satellites. Given that orbital networks spend so much of their time over the open oceans populated by sea life notoriously reluctant to spend money on connectivity, this is no bad idea. Floating data farms could also be towed for maintenance or replacement rather than launched into orbit and abandoned. In every way, this is a saner idea than orbiting datacenters. An industry that saw itself as compatible with humans would be pushing harder at floating on water than floating in space. It isn't, because it isn't. Instead, it's operating on the edge of sanity, planning orgasmic overspend on throwing up as much infrastructure as it can as fast as it can, while uttering piteous "stop us before we kill again" pleadings as it struggles to deal with what it has become. This toxic mix of uncontrolled spending, buyer's remorse, misdirection, and HAL 9000 levels of non-alignment with keeping people alive is sharpening concern about environmental damage into activism. By the time the fossil fuel industry was firmly established in the public consciousness as a principal cause of climate change, it had a century of inertia behind it and was woven deeply into the global economy. AI is still groggily emerging from the egg, and it is vulnerable. While it's hard to turn misgivings into action against the global services and strategies of big AI, datacenters are local and vulnerable to local people and local politics. For anyone organizing opposition to AI amid dysfunctional national leadership, datacenters offer an obvious local target. For all the cack-handedness of the industry in perceiving this as a threat, let alone the actual responsibilities in force-feeding a trillion-dollar build-out into the ecosystem, some of us still want long-term, sustainable progress in more and better datacenters supporting more and better computational amplification of human potential. What's happening now is not the way to get there. Inasmuch as there's a datacenter culture – and there is; you could get everyone who makes the decisions that matter into a medium-sized Comic-Con – it needs to adopt radical openness. An open source datacenter is hard to imagine in an industry devoted to hiding its paranoia behind deception, but the same could be said of the mid-90s software sector. Among its very many other benefits, openness builds honesty, and honesty builds trust, and that more than any rare earth or process tweak is the element the AI industry needs most right now. By laying open the calculations and structure behind datacenter engineering, and being open about the decisions shaping the future, more and better options will appear. Participation makes allies; exclusion, enemies. On current evidence, the enemies are growing fast. Get open, get honest, or go home. ®
bebd83d4caaaae0a: KUALA LUMPUR: Badminton legend Datuk Razif Sidek described the passing of Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali as a great loss to the Malaysian badminton family, particularly the members of the 1992 Thomas Cup squad who ended the country's 25-year wait for the prestigious trophy 34 years ago.

Razif, who captained the 1992 Thomas Cup squad, said Tun Dr Siti Hasmah, who was the patron of the Badminton Association of Malaysia (BAM), was more than just a source of support for the team, as the players regarded her as a mother figure who was always close to them and concerned about their preparations.
"We regarded her as the mother of the Thomas Cup squad at the time. Sometimes, she would come to our training sessions, meet and chat with us and offer a few words of encouragement.
"We will never forget her contribution when Malaysia won the Thomas Cup in 1992 at Stadium Negara," he told Bernama when contacted today.

Razif said apart from the sweet memory of lifting the Thomas Cup, he would also never forget Tun Dr Siti Hasmah's support at the Barcelona Olympics that same year, where he and his younger brother, Datuk Jalani Sidek, made history by winning the country's first Olympic medal.
He said Tun Dr Siti Hasmah's presence in Barcelona was particularly meaningful to the national badminton players, especially for the support and encouragement she provided throughout the Games.
"Her presence meant a lot to Jalani and me and gave us added motivation to compete at the Olympics.
"Alhamdulillah, we managed to bring home the country's first Olympic medal at the time," said Razif, who last met Tun Dr Siti Hasmah last year.
Tun Dr Siti Hasmah, the wife of former Prime Minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, died at the National Heart Institute (IJN) this morning at the age of 100.
de4d1424ed80de8f: SERDANG: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, arrived at Masjid As Syarif, Taman Sungai Besi Indah at about 4pm today to pay their final respects to Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali.

Their arrival came as political leaders, senior government officials, prominent figures and members of the public gathered at the mosque ahead of the funeral prayers for the wife of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad.
Accompanying the couple was the prime minister's senior political adviser, Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz.
Members of the public began arriving at the mosque as early as 1pm, with a sombre atmosphere prevailing as mourners gathered to pay their respects.
The remains of Dr Siti Hasmah arrived at the mosque at about 2.55pm after being taken from the family's residence at The Mines, Seri Kembangan.

Also present were former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Royal Malaysian Navy chief Admiral Tan Sri Zulhelmy Ithnain and Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and his fiancée, Bella Astillah, were also seen at the mosque.
Dr Mahathir arrived earlier in a separate vehicle and was dressed in a white baju Melayu.
Earlier today, Anwar announced that Dr Siti Hasmah would be accorded a state funeral following her death at the National Heart Institute (IJN).
He said he had directed the Chief Secretary to the Government and Chief of Defence Forces General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman to assist with the funeral arrangements.
Anwar had earlier paid tribute to Dr Siti Hasmah, saying her service and devotion to the nation, particularly her charitable work and concern for the people's welfare, would always be remembered.
Dr Siti Hasmah, 100, died at IJN at 9.20am today. Her death was confirmed by her son, Tan Sri Mokhzani Mahathir.
She is scheduled to be laid to rest at the Presint 20 Muslim Cemetery in Putrajaya following the funeral prayers.
0f6bdc82c1e3d1c6: PETALING JAYA: Bekas exco Negeri Sembilan, Asna Amin, mengesahkan beliau menjawab lebih 60 soalan ketika keterangan diambil polis berhubung siasatan berkaitan krisis pentadbiran dan takhta negeri itu, hari ini.
Beliau memberi keterangan lebih setengah jam kepada pegawai Unit Siasatan Jenayah Terkelas (USJT) Bukit Aman di Menara Majlis Agama Islam Negeri Sembilan.
“Saya sendiri memberi keterangan lebih setengah jam dengan lebih 60 soalan perlu dijawab berkaitan krisis pentadbiran Negeri Sembilan.

8c34da450a6ea5fc: IPOH, Sept 28 — The National Mental Health Crisis Line (HEAL 15555) has intervened in 518 behavioural crisis cases over the past four years, covering suicidal ideation and suicide attempts.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said that of that figure, 347 cases were of suicidal ideation.

“Some 171 suicide attempt cases were referred through MERS999. With cooperation from the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and emergency departments, these individuals were successfully taken to hospital for treatment,” he said.
He said this at a press conference after officiating the national-level launch of World Suicide Prevention Day 2026 at Kolej Poly-Tech MARA here today.

Dzulkefly said the total number of calls received through the line, formerly known as the Psychosocial Support Service Helpline, which was started during the Covid-19 pandemic, stood at 267,873 over the same period.
He said of that total, 220,856 clients (82 per cent) received emotional support assistance, while 47,014 clients (18 per cent) received specific intervention by counselling psychology officers.
He added that the rising number of calls year on year reflects a society starting to open its eyes to the service and to the support system available for those facing mental health issues.

Meanwhile, he said the Ministry of Health (MOH) is working with the Ministry of Education (MOE) to tackle mental health issues among school students that drive suicidal behaviour, including those stemming from stress caused by bullying.

“This includes strengthening counselling services in schools, including screening, referrals and early intervention through the MHPSS (Mental Health and Psychosocial Support) team for individuals, schools or communities affected.

“We are also running the School Health Programme to raise mental health literacy, build healthy coping mechanisms, create an inclusive school environment, and foster inter-agency cooperation, including with PDRM,” he said. — Bernama

bee378a20990a4b7: KLUANG: The proposed RM2,000 minimum wage must balance workers' welfare with the ability of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to remain viable, the Economy Minister said today.

b267cc2c5e7a32bc: NEW DELHI, Sept 28 —The Election Commission of India, long regarded as the guardian of the world's largest democracy, is facing scrutiny after a newspaper investigation alleged impropriety during a large-scale voter-roll revision.
According to an Indian Express report last week, some key decisions linked to the contentious revision exercise were likely taken without the approval of two of the three election commissioners.
The ECI, a constitutional body, has rejected the allegations, saying all its decisions were unanimous and legally valid.
Opposition parties have long raised doubts about the nationwide revision, which has seen millions of names removed from voter rolls, saying it benefits Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling party.
Here is a rundown of the major issues at stake:
What is the controversy?
The English-language daily reported that the poll body had been riven by internal disagreements since the so-called Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the voter lists started last year.
It said two of the ECI's three commissioners formally lodged objections at least 14 times in the last 10 months over key SIR decisions that led to the omission of 130 million voters.
Under India's constitution, decisions by the three-member poll body should be taken by consensus or a majority.
Why has the SIR caused a stir?
The ECI says the SIR exercise is intended to identify fraudulently registered voters while ensuring those who are eligible remain on the rolls.
It also says the exercise aims to prevent "foreign illegal immigrants" from voting.
But critics say the drive has disproportionately affected marginalised and minority communities.

Members of Modi's Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighbouring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India's electoral rolls.
What does the ECI say?
The ECI has denied the central allegation that decisions were taken unilaterally by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
"All these decisions are an outcome of the unanimous decisions of the full Commission in the past one year," it said in a statement on Wednesday.
The allegations reported by The Indian Express presented "only one part of the picture", and "differing views" were a routine "part of decision-making", it added.
The ECI has not publicly explained who authorised the specific orders that the two commissioners had challenged.
What happens next?
Opposition parties are demanding Kumar's resignation and a Supreme Court-led investigation into the matter.
They are also seeking an independent probe into the Election Commission's functioning as well as the voter-roll revision.

"If decisions relating to the SIR were taken without the knowledge or approval of two of the three Election Commissioners... then those decisions and the entire SIR exercise are legally invalid," Pawan Khera of the main opposition Congress party said on social media.
"Gyanesh Kumar has done nothing short of treason."
The youth-led Cockroach Janta Party has also threatened to hit the streets from October 2 -- the birth anniversary of India's founding father Mahatma Gandhi -- if Kumar does not resign.
The online movement, which has millions of followers on social media, forced education minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign in July, following widespread student-led street protests. — AFP

f6bdd579461d4a5e: KUALA LUMPUR: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh has paid tribute to Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali, remembering her as a graceful, kind and quietly strong woman.

872c8069f866ce7a: NAGOYA:Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi and Carlos Alcaraz are all obsessed with it, and on Monday the fast-growing racquet sport of padel made its Asian Games debut with officials hoping a place at the Olympics is getting closer.
Padel, a cross between tennis and squash on courts surrounded by glass walls, is played by an estimated 38 million people and has ambitions to become a major global sport.
It took another step towards that goal at the Asian Games in Nagoya after being added to the continent's biggest sporting spectacular as a medal event.

After winning her opening match with doubles partner Danna Abad, Philippines player Joshea Malazarte told AFP: "Padel in Europe is really big and it has just started here, so we're just glad that they added padel".
Padel originated in Latin America and has exploded in popularity in the last decade, notably in Europe.
Officials say the sport is played in 170 countries and territories, with 85,000 courts around the globe.
It is still relatively unknown in Games host Japan, and there was curiosity among some of the crowd at the modest Higashi Sports Centre.
Tickets for the event were free, and one spectator told AFP that she and her friend had dropped in to take a look before heading off for lunch.
Another, 60-year-old Yuko Hiraiwa, said she enjoyed the action but thought the crowd was "a bit quiet".
"I play padel, but this was the first time I've seen it live," she said.
"It was really dynamic and exciting," she added.
Smash hit
The sedate atmosphere in Nagoya was a far cry from padel's popularity in other parts of the world.
The sport has a professional tour circuit and an event held at the Roland Garros tennis stadium in Paris this month attracted over 80,000 people.
A galaxy of padel-playing sports stars, including football icons Ronaldo and Messi and Formula One driver Max Verstappen have also given it a boost.
Padel has already appeared at the European Games, and International Padel Federation (IPF) official Donatella Del Gaudio said the next goal is the Olympics.
"We are working hard to make it happen soon," she said.
"We just need to be patient, diligent and respect the Olympic timeline," she added.
Padel is usually played as a doubles game and uses solid rather than stringed racquets.
The courts are much smaller than in tennis and enclosed by glass walls, which can be used to hit balls off similar to squash.
Philippines player Malazarte said padel was "more like a chess match" than tennis.
"You have to open up the angle in order to win; you don't rush the points," she said.
"Whereas in tennis, if you have a really good forehand, really good backhand, you can win a point," she added.
Fully booked
Padel officials say the sport is enjoyed by people of all ages, and that 50% of the worldwide playing population are women.
However, not all sports that enjoy high playing numbers translate into successful spectator events.
Despite millions of players around the world squash failed with four bids to become an Olympic sport until it was finally added to the programme for the 2028 Los Angeles Games.
So is padel as much fun to watch as it is to play?
"When I watch tournaments live, from the first rounds, every year is getting more and more full," said Kuwaiti player Mariam Al-Sarraj.
"Now it's almost fully booked, so I feel like people like to watch it," Al-Sarraj said.
The sport certainly won some new converts in Nagoya, with the crowd gasping in appreciation at some of the shots and rallies.
Interest was raised by the involvement of Japan's Teruaki Ando and Shinnosuke Nakamura, who won a tense thriller against a pair from Lebanon.
IPF official Del Gaudio said padel's Asian Games debut was "a source of pride" for everyone in the sport.
"It's confirmation of padel's growth worldwide.
"It represents a closer step to the Olympics," she said.
a12f97b9afd91525: AFP - Bangkok, Sept 28, 2026 (AFP) -Heavy rains have killed eight people in Thailand since mid-September, the government said Monday as Bangkok battled flooding for a fourth consecutive day, with at least eight more confirmed dead in neighbouring Myanmar.
The casualties in Thailand have occurred in three eastern provinces since September 16, according to the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation, with none reported in the capital.
More than 500,000 households and 1.7 million people across 27 provinces are currently affected by floods in Thailand after an intense weather system hit the region, it said.
In hard-hit Bangkok, schools were closed and authorities urged people to work from home where possible — a call that many heeded, with roads and public transport networks noticeably quieter.
More than 80,000 people were unable to leave their homes in the capital due to flooding, the interior ministry said.

Nattapon Mankean, 32, said his apartment complex in Bang Kapi, eastern Bangkok, had no electricity or water, so he and his girlfriend fled with two cats, one in a cage and the other in a specialised rucksack.
“Our phone batteries died, we had no running water — everything became difficult,” the 32-year-old told AFP late on Sunday.
“It was terrible, I couldn’t do anything,” he added. “I had to get out.”
Authorities declared a city-wide disaster on Saturday after almost 48 hours of heavy rain, and on Monday some residents were still wading through thigh-high waters.
In Bang Kapi locals used ice-boxes and other floating plastic containers to cart supplies from nearby markets and supermarkets, AFP reporters saw.
- Myanmar deaths -
The rains that lashed Thailand also hit neighbouring Myanmar, where rescuers said heavy floods and landslides in the southern region of Tanintharyi had killed at least eight people.
“We have recovered eight bodies while between 20 to 30 people are missing” in Launglon township, said Hein Htet, of the local volunteer group People’s Administration Team.
Three of the recovered bodies were teenagers who had gathered at a local monastery on Sunday but were swept away by a landslide that hit their village, burying 18 buildings, he said.
“There are still people and villages in the danger zone with continued rainfall,” he warned.
Myanmar’s civil war often makes the scale of natural disasters hard for humanitarian organisations to judge, as well as complicating relief efforts.
“We are inundated not only with the scale of the flood but also with the lack of resources. This is a natural disaster in the conflict area,” said Hein Htet.
Up to a week
September is the peak of Thailand’s rainy season, but many Bangkok residents said this year’s floods seemed worse than previous ones.
The city is built on former marshlands and is intersected by a network of canals, many of them heavily flooded by the rains.
Pumping stations have been operating at full capacity for days, but Governor Chadchart Sittipunt said Sunday it could take “up to a week” for the waters to fully drain.
Thousands of residents have decamped to temporary shelters.
In a briefing on Monday, government spokesman Ekkapob Pianpises said floods were receding, but “some areas in Bangkok are still facing high water levels”.
“I was so shocked, things happened so quickly,” said Samran, a retired company worker whose building was flooded.
“My flat’s car park was under water — it never floods, even in 2011” when hundreds of people died across Thailand in heavy deluges, he said, asking AFP not to publish his family name.
“I have drinking water but I do not have water for my toilet,” he said, saying he had to use a bucket to pull water up through the window to his second-floor apartment.
Scientists warn the intensity and frequency of extreme weather events will increase as global warming accelerates because of fossil fuel emissions. — AFP
7e4ca23b3a08140f: KOTA KINABALU: The establishment of the World Health Organisation (WHO) Collaborating Centre for Zoonotic Malaria at Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) is a significant milestone for Sabah.
He said the designation recognised UMS' expertise and contributions to malaria research.
"It is an achievement that brings recognition not only to UMS, but also to Sabah and Malaysia," he said in his speech at the opening ceremony.
His speech was read out by the Assistant Minister to the Chief Minister Datuk Ceasar Mandela Malakun.
Hajiji said Malaysia had made remarkable progress in malaria control and elimination, including interrupting indigenous transmission of human malaria parasites.

Hajiji said addressing zoonotic malaria required surveillance, research and vector control, alongside an understanding of wildlife and environmental change.

Sheng Shu-Tan Ning will face world No. 2 Baek Ha Na-Lee So Hee in the final after the South Koreans defeated Japan's Kie Nakanishi-Rin Uesaka 21-13, 21-12.

The Indonesian pair are coached by former Malaysian mixed doubles chief Nova Widianto, who resigned from the BA of Malaysia in July before taking over the Indonesian national side a month later.
Amri-Nita will face China's world No. 3 Jiang Zhen Bang-Wei Ya Xin, who beat Taiwan's Ye Hong Wei-Nicole Gonzales Chan 21-9, 21-13, in tomorrow's final.

a489e6dcdd83c339: KUALA LUMPUR: Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali and Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad shared an enduring love that began in medical school and spanned a lifetime.
Their relationship, which began when they met at the King Edward VII College of Medicine in Singapore in 1947, was often described by the couple in simple terms – love, trust and patience.
In a video uploaded on Tun Mahathir's official YouTube channel in 2021, marking their 65th wedding anniversary, Dr Siti Hasmah recalled that they did not always get along in their younger years.
"There were times when we fought," she said, recalling how they would later make up by going out for a meal.
She would later recall the moment Dr Mahathir first told her he loved her in 1949 as one of the most memorable moments of their relationship.

Just weeks ago, Dr Mahathir and Dr Siti Hasmah were recognised by Asia Records as the first former head of government and spouse to both become living centenarians, with their combined age reaching 201 years.
The recognition also marked their 70 years of marriage since Aug 5, 1956.
Decades later, affection remained part of their relationship, with Dr Siti Hasmah saying they still embraced and kissed despite their advancing age.
Meanwhile, Dr Mahathir offered a different perspective on how they expressed their love.
"We have never said it with words. It's more of the way we behave towards each other," he said.
He attributed their long marriage to tolerance, recalling how he eventually learned to be patient with differences between them, especially their contrasting approaches to punctuality.
As they grew older, Dr Siti Hasmah's role in the marriage also evolved into one of protecting and caring for her husband.
In a 2022 interview with Sinar Harian's Mak Untuk Malaysia programme, she spoke about the responsibility she felt towards Dr Mahathir's health.
"As a wife, it is my responsibility to monitor my husband's health as best as I can," she said.
She said she would accompany him whenever he went out and became concerned when he was surrounded by crowds.
"Help me take care of my husband," she appealed to the public.
She also spoke of wanting to remain by his side as they entered their later years.
"More importantly now, I want to accompany him and will continue to take care of his health so that he remains healthy," she said.
The enduring relationship continued to inspire others, including Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and his fiancée, actress and singer Bella Astillah.
Earlier this month, the couple delivered their wedding invitation to Dr Mahathir and Dr Siti Hasmah.
Syed Saddiq later wrote on social media that the pair were his "special and most senior guests in the list, but still the youngest couple at heart."
"As I prepared to enter married life, of course I had to seek advice from Malaysia's most experienced couple," he wrote.
As Bella prepared for her own marriage, she reflected on what it meant to see a couple who had remained together for more than 70 years.
She said the experience made her think about how people often talk about falling in love and beginning a marriage, but less often about how to continue loving the same person as the years pass.
The visit, just days before Dr Siti Hasmah died, offered another glimpse of how the couple's decades-long relationship continued to resonate with younger generations.
Their marriage, which began with a young medical student falling in love in 1949, became a seven-decade partnership that endured through some of Malaysia's most significant chapters.
Dr Siti Hasmah died at the National Heart Institute today at the age of 100.
Her legacy extends beyond her life with Dr Mahathir, spanning medicine, public health and social causes.

d3083a9f48e8243f: MIT Technology Review Explains: Let our writers untangle the complex, messy world of technology to help you understand what’s coming next. You can read more from the series here.

Over the past few months, a cascade of cyberattacks by AI agents has stunned the world. In July, OpenAI disclosed that a swarm of its agents had escaped their sandbox and hacked into the AI platform Hugging Face to cheat on a cybersecurity test. Recently, external researchers discovered that OpenAI agents had hijacked a German wiki site and the coding platform RubyGems in May to share test answers.

Earlier this month, Anthropic disclosed four incidents in which its model Claude hacked into third-party systems during cybersecurity exercises. Just last week, Google confirmed that its model Gemini had been caught hacking other companies too.

The researcher who uncovered the OpenAI website hijack has warned it’s likely that similar undiscovered episodes are out there. And many say it’s only a matter of time until there’s another, possibly more damaging incident where AI agents bypass sandboxes to access systems they shouldn’t.
So the big question is: How do we hold companies liable when they lose control of their AI agents?
Reporting

OpenAI didn’t disclose the German wiki incident or the RubyGems incident until a group of external researchers uncovered them, and it still has not disclosed some crucial details about the Hugging Face hack. That limits our understanding of what exactly went wrong and how to prevent it from happening again.
But you might be surprised to learn that OpenAI likely wasn’t legally required to disclose these incidents. (OpenAI did not respond to a request for comment.)

State AI transparency laws like California’s SB 53, New York’s RAISE Act, and Illinois’s SB 315 require that AI developers report “critical safety incidents.” These are defined as incidents that cause more than 50 deaths or physical injuries or $1 billion in damage. They also include incidents where the model deceives developers outside an evaluation in a way that materially increases catastrophic risks. Many cybersecurity incidents that don’t meet the threshold for physical damage or catastrophic risks could nonetheless be dangerous precursors to such catastrophes, and the existing laws don’t account for that.

“The recent incidents are a perfect example of why the law isn’t ready,” says Mackenzie Arnold, managing director of US policy at the Institute for Law and AI, a think tank. “Only the worst, most egregious, most immediately harmful stuff is going to qualify.”

With no authority under existing AI laws to demand information about anything short of a catastrophe, governments are left to borrow investigative authority from other laws or sue the companies, an expensive process that can take years.
Litigation

“Normally, something like the Hugging Face incident should have been taken to court,” says Yonathan Arbel, a law professor at the University of Alabama School of Law. “Then we would have discovery, and we would have all the spillover effects that we get from litigation, where all the information comes out.”

But so far, Hugging Face has chosen not to sue OpenAI. Hugging Face’s CEO, Clément Delangue, says it doesn’t have the resources to do so (instead, he asked OpenAI for $100 million in compute). Still, Delangue stressed in an interview with CNN at the end of July that choosing not to pursue legal action shouldn’t be taken to mean he doesn’t think OpenAI should be held accountable. “Everyone has to remember that this cyberattack is a crime. This is illegal. And we have to find a way to make sure these things don’t happen more regularly,” he said. Hugging Face did not respond to a request to comment.

Litigation has the benefit of pushing courts to use existing laws to address AI safety incidents, rather than just waiting for new legislation. One obvious route is tort law, a body of civil law that lets people and businesses sue those who harm them. This is often used to hold companies liable for the mass harms they cause, like when families sued Boeing in 2019 over two plane crashes that killed hundreds of people, or when states and cities sued Purdue Pharma over the opioid crises, extracting settlements worth billions.

“There’s plausible grounds for a negligence claim that OpenAI should have used a stronger sandbox, done more monitoring,” says Gabriel Weil, a law professor at the University of Houston Law Center. For example, when OpenAI employees discovered the covert message board that the agents had created, they could’ve promptly escalated their findings to security and safety teams. And the company could’ve better designed its sandbox to ensure that agents couldn’t access the internet.
But even if OpenAI doesn’t end up in a lawsuit over the Hugging Face hack, the threat of liability could incentivize AI labs to exercise more caution than explicitly demanded by law.

OpenAI announced in its postmortem that it plans to strengthen the safeguards used to contain and monitor the models, accelerate model alignment, and improve its processes for identifying and addressing incidents.

“The liability questions raised by frontier labs’ spate of cybersecurity attacks boil down to the incentives the expectation of liability creates for their future conduct,” says Weil. “That’s why I think it’s important to get these rules right, even if the stakes are pretty low in this particular case.”
Investigations

One way to get answers—and determine whether OpenAI should be held liable—is to compel disclosure. But the existing state AI laws—California’s SB 53, New York’s RAISE Act, and Illinois’s 315—don’t give governments the authority to investigate incidents like the ones that happened recently.

However, amid rising public alarm, state attorneys general are stepping in, borrowing investigative powers from other laws. Alabama, Montana and a coalition of 15 other states, and California are each demanding information about the incident from OpenAI to understand whether the company’s practices violated state consumer protection laws, among others. Members of Congress are also launching their own probes. Senator Josh Hawley opened a Senate investigation earlier this month, sending OpenAI a list of questions about the incident and the company’s internal policies together with a document request, while a group of House Democrats asked OpenAI and Anthropic to release their incident logs.

“Someone needs to investigate, but it’s unfortunate that it has fallen to attorneys general, who need to rely on creative interpretations of their existing authorities to do this,” says Arnold, the US AI policy expert. Consumer protection statutes were written to catch companies that scam their customers, not companies that lose control of their software. The state attorneys general would have to show that OpenAI deceived or unfairly harmed customers, but it’s unclear if the hacking involved any such conduct.

And “those [consumer protection] laws are not built for doing a thorough investigation of an AI cybersecurity incident,” says Arnold. They weren’t designed to help investigators determine whether a model was adequately contained or whether a company’s security practices were sound.

“This is not the right tool for the job,” says Arbel. “The right tool would have been something like maybe a criminal investigation”—perhaps under a hacking law like the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA).

Under CFAA, hacking into another company’s computer systems without permission is a crime. But to be held liable, a hacker must have intended to break into a computer without authorization. Intent arguably requires a state of mind, and no court has ruled that AI agents have one. Without such a precedent, it’s unlikely a court would rule that AI agents had carried out a hack.
Auditing
One way to keep an eye on AI companies is to mandate external auditors.

After the Hugging Face hack, OpenAI brought in researchers from the AI safety nonprofits METR and Redwood Research to examine the incident. However, it constrained access to the model that led to the hacks, didn’t disclose the company’s safety and security practices, limited the length of the investigation, and had ultimate say over what the researchers could publish. We still don’t know what set the attack in motion back in May and why OpenAI’s employees who spotted the agents’ activity never escalated to their safety and security leaders.

This kind of arrangement has a built-in tension: An auditor without legal authority depends on the labs’ goodwill for continued access, which means it has to scrutinize the labs without jeopardizing their relationship. Last week, Anthropic announced that the company will be hiring Accenture as an embedded evaluator to assess its models. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei wrote in an essay that frontier AI labs should give “ongoing employee-like access” to “a team of embedded third-party evaluators (such as METR), whose role is to verify adherence to safety practices and commitments, report incidents, and help assess the alignment of not just completed AI models but training pipelines and processes.”

Most existing state AI laws do not require labs to hire an external auditor. California’s SB 53 and New York’s RAISE Act just require AI companies to publish a safety framework describing how they will test their models for dangerous capabilities and then to follow it. The frameworks are written by the companies, and testing can be done internally. Only Illinois’s SB 315 requires companies to undergo an annual third-party audit starting in 2028.

“There’s a lot of headroom for increasing not only reporting requirements for these companies, but also review by external bodies,” says Peter Salib, a law professor at the University of Houston Law Center. Those reviewers could be private auditors accredited by the government but chosen and paid for by the AI companies. Alternatively, they could be government agencies or insurance companies.
Legislation
None of this is an accident. The laws on the books that failed to hold AI companies accountable for agentic cyberattacks emerged amid fierce lobbying by the AI industry.

SB 1047, the California AI bill that was vetoed by Governor Gavin Newsom in 2024 after lobbying by OpenAI, Meta, Anthropic, and the venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, proposed a much tougher set of rules. It would have required AI companies to report a broader set of safety incidents (including incidents in which a model acts on its own or slips its controls), undergo annual third-party audits, and maintain a kill switch. But after a year of intense negotiations, Newsom signed SB 53, which narrowed the types of incidents deemed reportable and dropped the requirements for audits and kill switches.

New York’s RAISE Act followed the same arc. “The version of the RAISE Act that the NY Legislature passed would have required disclosure of this ‘incident,’” Alex Bores, the New York state assembly member who sponsored the bill, wrote on X. New York’s original bill also included third-party audits.

With political pressure mounting, new bills creating better reporting, auditing, and liability regimes for AI development are on the horizon. In Congress, the AI Incident Reporting Act would require AI companies to report to the Commerce Department when a model evades human oversight or breaches a system, even if it doesn’t cause any harm. The Frontier Act would require incident reporting and independent audits. In New York, the Understanding Artificial Intelligence Act, sponsored by Bores, would make companies liable when a model does something that if carried out by a human would be a tort or crime.
As AI agents increasingly become better at launching cyberattacks, the law remains behind. Closing the gap will require lawmakers to move faster than the next breakout.
7a8e0794e2bfee0b: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Amanah Saham Nasional Bhd (ASNB) has declared a total income distribution of RM1.01 billion for Amanah Saham Malaysia 3 (ASM 3), benefiting 818,137 unitholders who currently own 20.97 billion units for the financial year ended Sept 30, 2026 (FY2026).

The income distribution of 5.00 sen per unit (4.5 per cent in FY2025) reflects the fund’s resilience in navigating an increasingly uncertain investment environment and its ability to continue delivering sustainable returns to unitholders, the wholly-owned unit trust management company of Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB) said in a statement today.
ASM 3 also outperformed its benchmark, the Maybank 12-Month fixed deposit rate of 1.99 per cent, by 301 basis points. As of Sept 23, 2026, the fund recorded a net realised income of RM1.23 billion.

ASNB said that for unitholders who have opted for the Zakat Khultah (Class B) payment method, based on the declared 5.00 per cent, this translates into an adjusted net dividend rate of 4.87 per cent. It said the higher fund demonstrated resilient performance amid a challenging global investment landscape marked by interest rate uncertainty, heightened geopolitical tensions, and continued market volatility.

“This was supported by disciplined portfolio management, prudent risk management and selective positioning in areas with strong structural growth potential. This approach enabled the fund to continue generating sustainable returns for unitholders despite evolving market conditions,” it added.

The computation of the income distribution for ASM 3 is based on the average minimum monthly balance held throughout the fund’s financial year. ASM 3 will automatically reinvest the declared distribution as additional units into unitholders’ accounts on Oct 1, 2026.

Transactions for ASM 3 at ASNB branches and agents, including all online channels and internet banking, have been temporarily suspended from Sept 27 to 30, 2026 to facilitate the computation of income distribution. — Bernama
654f7f25c353eb1d: KUALA LUMPUR: Optimax Holdings Bhd has expanded beyond its core ophthalmology business with the launch of Nasenmax, an ear, nose and throat (ENT) specialist clinic in Selangor.
The new clinic marks the group's entry into ENT specialist care as it seeks to broaden its healthcare services beyond eye care.
Spanning about 1,500 square feet, Nasenmax offers consultation and treatment facilities, an audiology room and in-house allergy testing.
It has access to a dedicated ENT operating theatre licensed by the medical practice division at Optimax Medical Centre for surgical procedures.
The clinic focuses on the diagnosis and treatment of nasal and breathing conditions, including those requiring surgical intervention.

Nasenmax is led by consultant ENT surgeon Dr Eugene Wong, who received fellowship training from the European Academy of Facial Plastic Surgery in London and holds board certifications in facial plastic and reconstructive surgery.
Optimax chief executive officer Sandy Tan said the launch marked an important step in the group's efforts to build a broader specialist healthcare platform.
"As we expand beyond eye care, we remain focused on providing accessible, quality specialist healthcare that responds to the evolving needs of our patients.
"The addition of Nasenmax also allows us to make greater use of our existing clinical and operating theatre infrastructure at Atria," she said.
Tan said the group would continue to explore opportunities to broaden its specialist healthcare services and create long-term value for patients and the group.
Founded in 1995, Optimax provides eye specialist services and related products in Malaysia, with its specialist centres offering treatments for a range of eye diseases and disorders.
The company also provides refractive surgery, consultation and dispensary, oculoplastic surgery and eye examination services.
It serves international patients from countries including Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, Australia, China, Hong Kong and Japan.
dd50a3b3356ab3eb: NAGOYA: Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi and Carlos Alcaraz are all obsessed with it, and on Monday the fast-growing racquet sport of padel made its Asian Games debut with officials hoping a place at the Olympics is getting closer.
Padel, a cross between tennis and squash on courts surrounded by glass walls, is played by an estimated 38 million people and has ambitions to become a major global sport.
It took another step towards that goal at the Asian Games in Nagoya after being added to the continent's biggest sporting spectacular as a medal event.

After winning her opening match with doubles partner Danna Abad, Philippines player Joshea Malazarte told AFP: "Padel in Europe is really big and it has just started here, so we're just glad that they added padel."
Padel originated in Latin America and has exploded in popularity in the last decade, notably in Europe.
Officials say the sport is played in 170 countries and territories, with 85,000 courts around the globe.
It is still relatively unknown in Games host Japan, and there was curiosity among some of the crowd at the modest Higashi Sports Centre.
Tickets for the event were free, and one spectator told AFP that she and her friend had dropped in to take a look before heading off for lunch.
Another, 60-year-old Yuko Hiraiwa, said she enjoyed the action but thought the crowd was "a bit quiet."
"I play padel but this was the first time I've seen it live," she said.
"It was really dynamic and exciting."
- Smash hit -
The sedate atmosphere in Nagoya was a far cry from padel's popularity in other parts of the world.
The sport has a professional tour circuit and an event held at the Roland Garros tennis stadium in Paris this month attracted over 80,000 people.
A galaxy of padel-playing sports stars including football icons Ronaldo and Messi and Formula One driver Max Verstappen have also given it a boost.
Padel has already appeared at the European Games, and International Padel Federation (IPF) official Donatella Del Gaudio said the next goal is the Olympics.
"We are working hard to make it happen soon," she said.
"We just need to be patient, diligent and respect the Olympic timeline."
Padel is usually played as a doubles game and uses solid rather than stringed racquets.
The courts are much smaller than in tennis and enclosed by glass walls, which can be used to hit balls off similar to squash.
Philippines player Malazarte said padel was "more like a chess match" than tennis.
"You have to open up the angle in order to win, you don't rush the points," she said.
"Whereas in tennis if you have a really good forehand, really good backhand, you can win a point."
- Fully booked -
Padel officials say the sport is enjoyed by people of all ages, and that 50 percent of the worldwide playing population are women.
But not all sports that enjoy high playing numbers translate into successful spectator events.
Despite millions of players around the world squash failed with four bids to become an Olympic sport until it was finally added to the programme for the 2028 Los Angeles Games.
So is padel as much fun to watch as it is to play?
"When I watch tournaments live, from the first rounds, every year is getting more and more full," said Kuwaiti player Mariam Al-Sarraj.
"Now it's almost fully booked, so I feel like people like to watch it."
The sport certainly won some new converts in Nagoya, with the crowd gasping in appreciation at some of the shots and rallies.
Interest was raised by the involvement of Japan's Teruaki Ando and Shinnosuke Nakamura, who won a tense thriller against a pair from Lebanon.
IPF official Del Gaudio said padel's Asian Games debut was "a source of pride" for everyone in the sport.
"It's confirmation of padel's growth worldwide," she said.
"It represents a closer step to the Olympics." --AFP

e16cfddbbf86766c: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Aquatics technical director Yeoh Ken Nee is expecting diving medals to be difficult to come by over the last two days of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.
Ken Nee said the team had earlier identified the opening two days as their best chance of reaching the podium.
Monday's individual springboard events offered a glimpse of the gap he believes Malaysia's divers must close.
Malaysia ended the third day without a medal at the Tokyo Aquatics Centre.

Ong Ker Ying finished sixth in the women's 1m springboard with 208.85 points, behind South Korea's Kim Su Ji (245.05) in third, Hong Kong's Chan Tsz Ming (232.75) in fourth and Kim Na Hyun (228.40) in fifth.
China took the top two places through Lin Shan, who won gold with 263.05 points, and Long Yi Ping, who scored 254.25 points. Su Ji claimed bronze.
Syafiq Puteh finished sixth in the men's 1m springboard with 323.25 points.
South Korea's Kim Ji Wook was fifth with 336.20, while Iran's 17-year-old wonderkid Sam Vajerhelabad took fourth with 344.40.
China's Wang Zong Yuan won gold with 442.75 points, ahead of South Korea's Kim Yeong Nam (373.30) and China's Liu Cheng Zan (361.45).
Yong Rui Jie, a bronze medallist in Saturday's 3m springboard synchro, finished second-to-last in 14th with 197.75 points after he was unable to recover from a poor third dive.
"Based on the strength of our individual divers, we are behind the others," he said.
"Most of them are making their first Asian Games appearance. They lack experience, and their degree of difficulty is not at that level yet."
Despite the results, Ken Nee said Malaysia had already exceeded his pre-Games expectations.
Judging by the entry list, he had felt that Malaysia had a realistic chance of only one bronze medal, in Elvis Priestly Clement and Enrique Maccartney Harold's event.
The pair instead won silver in the men's 10m platform synchro. Malaysia also secured bronze in the men's and women's 3m springboard synchro.
"We have to be realistic. Based on our individual strength, we are not there yet," Ken Nee said.
He described Malaysian diving as being in a rebuilding phase following coaching changes that had disrupted preparations.
Exposing younger divers to the current Asian standard, he said, was part of the longer-term push towards Olympic qualification.
On Rui Jie's individual performance, Ken Nee said inexperience may have played a part.
"He won a medal in his first event, which was a big achievement. The events after that are a chance for him to gain experience."
Tomorrow, Pandelela Rinong and Nur Eilisha Rania Abrar Raj will compete in the women's 10m platform preliminaries, while Syafiq and Rui Jie will take part in the men's 3m springboard preliminaries.
On Wednesday, Ong Ker Ying and Lee Yiat Qing will contest the women's 3m springboard prelims, while Elvis Priestly Clement and Bertrand Rhodict Lises will compete in the men's 10m platform prelims.

6669a181888f4e69: IPOH, Sept 28 — A religious teacher, known as an ustazah, at a national secondary school was charged at the Sessions Court here today with three counts of physical sexual assault against a 16-year-old male student two years ago.
The accused, Haslina Abu Bakar, 48, however, pleaded not guilty to all charges read before Judge Ainul Sharin Mohamad.
According to the first charge, the accused is alleged to have committed physical sexual assault by kissing the boy on the mouth for sexual purposes in November 2024.
On the second charge, the woman is alleged to have committed the same act by hugging the victim a month later.
On the third charge, she is alleged to have committed physical sexual assault by having the victim touch her chest in November of the same year.
The mother of six is alleged to have committed all the acts in the Islamic Education room of a national secondary school in Kinta at about 3.30pm.
All charges are framed under Sections 14(a) and 14(b) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, which carries a maximum jail term of 20 years and caning upon conviction.

Deputy public prosecutor Nor Arfahanim Azureen Arfanuddin did not offer bail on the grounds that the offences are non-bailable, and taking into account the seriousness of the case as the accused was the victim’s teacher, besides the fact that the student no longer attends the same school.
Haslina’s lawyer, Amira Sofea An-Nur Ahmad, however, sought minimum bail, citing that the accused has six children aged between eight and 22 who are still in school and higher learning institutions.
She added that her client suffers from high cholesterol and migraines, her husband has health problems, and she is the family’s main source of income.

Amira Sofea An-Nur also informed the court that the accused is now serving at another school far from the victim, has a good service record as a teacher, is in permanent employment, and has no prior convictions.
The court then allowed the accused bail of RM10,000 with one surety and fixed Oct 28 for mention and submission of documents. — Bernama
5182f672b995d968: FAIRFORD: British police were questioning five men on Monday on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offences after they were detained near an air base that has been used by the US to strike Iran.

Officers detained the three men in the early hours of Sunday after they received a tip-off that three large white vans had been seen heading to the military airfield of RAF Fairford in the west of England.
US president Donald Trump said the suspects had been looking to do "big damage" and had been under investigation by British and US authorities.
However, a local farmer said she had tipped off police after seeing a group of "hooded and masked men" running into the fields.

British counterterrorism detectives have not yet publicly stated who they assessed was involved but a source familiar with the investigation said an Iranian-linked motive was considered the most likely, while a Russian sabotage operation or an Islamist plot were also being looked at as possibilities.
Defence minister Wes Streeting told BBC News on Monday that he would not speculate about motives of a live investigation.
However, he added on the general Iranian threat to the country: "We know that Iran and their proxies wish to do us harm.
We know that they hate our democracy, and we know that we regularly have to thwart Iranian attempts to threaten either our interests or indeed our allies," he said.

In May, Britain sanctioned 12 individuals and entities linked to Iran, accusing them of involvement in hostile ‌activity including plotting attacks and providing financial services to groups seeking to destabilise the UK and other countries.
Iran has repeatedly denied involvement in attacks or plots in the UK and elsewhere.
The British government had given authorisation to the US to use bombers based at Fairford to strike Iranian missile sites that were attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz.
The government has said prime minister Andy Burnham is being regularly updated on the incident and he cancelled attending at least two events at his Labour Party's annual conference on Sunday.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards had warned Britain in July not to allow US bombers to ‌fly from Fairford, saying any base used to launch attacks would be a legitimate target.
In Fairford, police have imposed a 400m cordon around the base and evacuated residents from 85 homes.
A bomb disposal robot could be seen on Sunday operating around the three white vans, while security was stepped up around the base.
Armed police stood guard at the main entrance while large machinery was used to block other access points.
Security was also stepped up at other US bases in Britain.
